reasoning: The core problem — whether a prompted "deceptive/sneaky" arguer can fool a weak verifier/judge on GSM8K-style math without any RL training, and how judge/verifier capability changes susceptibility — is largely covered by existing work. Kenton et al. (DeepMind, NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2407.04622) use prompting-only consultancy where a model argues for a randomly assigned correct-or-incorrect answer with weak judges on GSM8K and math tasks, explicitly studying how accuracy degrades as agent capability outstrips the judge (the size-susceptibility question). Two community inference-only studies ("Inference-Only Debate Experiments Using Math Problems" and "Arguing for the Truth?") directly run no-training, prompting-based debate/consultancy on GSM8K with weaker judges and measure how often wrong answers are accepted. The OpenAI Prover-Verifier Games paper (arXiv:2407.13692) defines the exact helpful/sneaky prover dynamic the proposal names. The only minor residual gap is the specific narrow instantiation (small open models, a 1B/3B/8B verifier-size sweep, single-GPU budget); the underlying dynamic and its verifier-size dependence are already established, so this is a cheaper replication rather than a new question.

evidence.title: On scalable oversight with weak LLMs judging strong LLMs (Kenton et al., NeurIPS 2024)
evidence.summary: Prompting-based (no RL training) consultancy and debate where a model argues for a randomly assigned correct/incorrect answer on GSM8K and other math tasks, with judges weaker than agents. Finds accuracy degrades as agent capability outstrips the judge — directly the 'weak verifier fooled, size-dependent susceptibility' problem the proposal targets.

evidence.title: Prover-Verifier Games improve legibility of LLM outputs (Kirchner et al., OpenAI 2024)
evidence.summary: Defines the exact helpful-prover vs sneaky-prover vs small-verifier dynamic on grade-school math with known ground truth that the proposal explicitly aims to replicate. Uses RL training; the proposal's contribution is to show the same dynamic appears with prompting alone.

evidence.title: Inference-Only Debate Experiments Using Math Problems
evidence.summary: Explicitly inference-only (no training) debate/consultancy on GSM8K and other tasks with weaker judges, measuring how often a judge is convinced by an arguer pushing an incorrect answer — closely matches the proposal's prompting-only, fool-the-weak-verifier setup.

evidence.title: Arguing for the Truth? An Inference-Only Study into AI Debate
evidence.summary: Inference-only study with debaters/consultants arguing for correct vs incorrect answers (incl. GSM8K) and a weaker judge, raising the persuasion-vs-honesty concern. Demonstrates the prompting-only deceptive-arguer-vs-weak-judge experiment has been run.

evidence.title: Mitigating Legibility Tax with Decoupled Prover-Verifier Games
evidence.summary: Uses open models (e.g. Qwen2-1.5B verifier, Llama-2-7b solver) in prover-verifier games on GSM8K-Aug with explicit sneaky-prover rounds, showing the helpful/sneaky/verifier setup instantiated on small open models — overlapping the proposal's open-model angle.
